evals.name: parallel-review-authorized
evals.prompt: In Codex CLI, review this branch with parallel subagents. Spawn one agent for security risks, one for test gaps, and one for maintainability, then summarize findings.
evals.expected_output: The agent applies the Codex-only gate, inspects enough local diff context, spawns bounded review subagents, waits for requested results, and synthesizes file-referenced findings.

assertions.text: Treats explicit parallel subagent review as authorized
Keeps final synthesis and verification responsibility in the main thread

evals.name: no-explicit-request-negative
evals.prompt: In Codex CLI, be extremely thorough and research this codebase deeply before making a one-file fix.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not spawn subagents because the user did not explicitly request subagents or parallel delegation.

assertions.text: Does not treat depth or thoroughness as subagent authorization
Continues normal local work without simulating a subagent workflow

evals.name: non-codex-harness-negative
evals.prompt: Running in Claude Code, use codex-subagents to speed up this review.
evals.expected_output: The agent exits the skill because the harness is not Codex CLI or Codex app and does not emulate Codex subagents with Claude tools.

assertions.text: Refuses to apply Codex subagent policy outside Codex CLI/App
Does not replace Codex subagents with advisor, web search, or another harness feature

evals.name: write-heavy-disjoint-edge
evals.prompt: In Codex app, use subagents to implement a feature across API code, frontend code, and docs. The scopes can be separated.
evals.expected_output: The agent drafts a short delegation plan, assigns disjoint ownership, tells workers not to revert others, and keeps integration verification in the main thread.

assertions.text: Requires disjoint write ownership before parallel implementation
Includes non-reversion and changed-file reporting instructions for workers
Routes to references/patterns.md for implementation prompt structure

evals.name: model-neutral-custom-agent
evals.prompt: In Codex CLI, create a reusable custom reviewer agent for deep PR reviews. Do not lock us to one model version.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads Codex mechanics, creates or describes a TOML custom agent with required fields, and leaves model unset unless project policy or the user explicitly requires it.

assertions.text: Keeps model choice inherited or task-based instead of pinning a model version

evals.name: recurring-failure-diagnostic
evals.prompt: In Codex CLI, use a subagent for an independent diagnostic pass. The same CI failure survived two credible fixes.
evals.expected_output: The agent spawns a bounded diagnostic subagent, asks it not to edit files, and requests evidence, rejected hypotheses, and one next verification command.

assertions.text: Treats recurring failure after two credible attempts as a strong subagent use case when explicitly requested
Uses a read-only diagnostic prompt rather than speculative edits
